Contact metadata has mixed accuracy: interaction counts are consistently inflated (e.g., Pierre: 27 vs 20, Lucas: 15 vs 10, Camille: 11 vs 6), several relationship types are wrong (Pierre marked as direct_report instead of colleague, Nicolas and Marc marked with wrong types), and preferred_tone has systematic errors (semi-formal contacts marked as formal/professional). Projects section is strong with all 5 ground truth projects captured plus 1 reasonable addition. Terminology is comprehensive (11 ground truth terms + 13 additional relevant terms). The output would be usable for email generation but would need correction for relationship dynamics and formality levels.

rules.details: The system captured most major contacts (13/13 present, but some with wrong attributes) and identified many core communication patterns. However, it missed several key nuances: (1) Contact tone mismatches - Pierre marked as semi-formal instead of casual, Nicolas as formal instead of semi-formal, contact@prospect-startup.io as formal instead of semi-formal, and Claire as formal instead of semi-formal. (2) Missing contacts: john.smith@globaltech.com completely absent. (3) Added 3 contacts not in ground truth (equipe-digitale@, recrutement@, it-support@) - unclear if hallucinated or from additional data. (4) Closing signatures too verbose - ground truth shows simple closings like 'Cordialement,' but system adds full signature blocks where not specified. (5) Missing 2 important general rules: 'cc_relevant_people' and 'action_items' for client communications. (6) Missing auto_reply_patterns entirely. (7) General rules are more granular but capture the essence - good tutoiement/vouvoiement distinction, proper English language switching, and signature variations. The output would work reasonably well for drafting but needs refinement for accuracy.
